does: Takes the next video name from the movie player's queue, makes it the current one, looks its file up (the body of code:ls::VideoManager::LoadVideo, inlined: code:unplaced::FindVideoFile, then the player's loader at slot 1) and starts it; a name whose file is not found is reported stopped and the next one is tried.

evidence.says: same shape as the macOS build's ecl::VideoManager::NextVideo: pops the FixedString queue at +0x18 (count +0x24, head +0x28, tail +0x2c), copies the name into +0x30 and +0x34, calls the file lookup with the client's ModManager (EoCClient+0x140) and the player's virtual at slot 1; on failure calls the stopped broadcast bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x1BBC1C0

Osi.MoviePlay(host,'Splash_Logo_Larian',1) on the server in a test level: write watches on the client's movie player (ecl::GameControl+0x190) caught +0x24 going 1->0 at bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x1BBBDAC and +0x30 going from none to the played name at bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x1BBBDE2, both inside this function; a count-only probe saw code:unplaced::FindVideoFile called once from bg3_dx11.exe@25605617+0x1BBBE6E inside it; the Larian clip then showed in the game window
The macOS build's symbols hold this name; nothing but the name ties it to this function
